title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Throughout, ρ(g) = R g R^{-1} is the inner automorphism of GL(2, Ẑ_ℓ) given by a fixed matrix R of order 3 modulo scalars, with R^3 = ±1. Writing R for this matrix and ρ for the automorphism is my notation, not Grothendieck's.

Key identity. One has g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = (gR)^3 R^{-3}. So equation (87), g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = 1, says exactly that h := gR satisfies h^3 = R^3. In other words, solving (87) is the same as finding the 'twisted cube roots' of R^3 in the coset GL₂·R. Equivalently, (87) is the cocycle condition for the Z/3-action generated by ρ. This is a linear (abelianized / GL₂) model of the order-3 relation in Grothendieck's 'équation des lacets', i.e. the analogue of Drinfeld's GT relation (II), with ρ the cyclic permutation of order 3.

Which normalisation. The formulas on the page, (90) on the previous page and the remark g^3 = ρ^{-3} = -1 on the next page all fit R = [[0,1],[-1,1]], which has R^3 = -1. Then gR = [[-b, a+b], [-d, c+d]], with trace t = c + d - b and determinant δ = ad - bc.

Solving with Cayley–Hamilton. From h² = t h - δ one gets h^3 = (t² - δ) h - tδ. The condition h^3 = -1 then splits into two cases.
(i) h is a scalar λ with λ^3 = -1 and λ² = δ. This forces δ^3 = 1 and λ = -δ^{-1}. Hence g = -δ' R^{-1} = δ' [[-1,1],[-1,0]], with δ' = δ^{-1} = δ². This is case 2° and matches (90) on the previous page.
(ii) h is not scalar. Then t² = δ and tδ = 1, so t = δ' and δ^3 = 1. This is case 1°: c + d - b = δ'.

The two cases are disjoint. In case 2° the trace equals -2δ', and -2δ' ≠ δ' because 3δ' ≠ 0 in Z_ℓ.

Corollary, case 1° with a + b ≠ 0. Then d = b - c + δ'. Substituting into ad - bc = δ gives c(a+b) = a(b + δ') - δ, which is the formula on the page.

Corollary, case 1° with a + b = 0. Then b = -a, and the determinant condition becomes a² - aδ' + δ = 0. Put a = -uδ' and use δ^3 = 1: this reduces to u² + u + 1 = 0. Hence g = [[-uδ', uδ'], [c, -δ'u² - c]] with u a primitive cube root of unity.

Arithmetic remarks (not stated on the page).
- Over Z_ℓ, the condition δ^3 = 1 is nontrivial only when ℓ ≡ 1 mod 3.
- The family with a + b = 0 exists only when ℓ ≡ 1 mod 3.
- The next page counts parameters: the three cases give families with 2, 1 and 0 parameters. It also raises the question of whether every solution is a 'coboundary' λ₀ ρ(λ₀)^{-1}. That is the question of triviality of nonabelian H¹(Z/3, SL₂(Ẑ_ℓ)), possibly twisted.
errors: Case 1° as transcribed, 'c+d-b=1', contradicts the corollary, which uses d = b - c + 1/δ. The correct condition is c + d - b = δ' = 1/δ. Either the '1' is a slip of the pen or it is a misreading of '1/δ'.

Case 2° matrix: the derivation and (90) on the previous page give g = -δ'R^{-1} = δ'[[-1,1],[-1,0]] = [[-δ', δ'], [-δ', 0]]. As transcribed, '-δ'(-1 1; 1 0)' would put +δ' in the lower-left entry, a sign inconsistency (with the transcribed bracket, the identity '-δ'(−1 1; 1 0) = -δ'ρ^{-1}' cannot hold for an R of order 3 mod scalars). It is probably a sign slip, or the bracket should read (1 -1; 1 0) = R^{-1}.
The second family should read d = -δ'u' - c. The transcription has '-δu'-c'; checking against d = b - c + δ' gives δ'(u+1) - c = -δ'u² - c.
Not stated on the page: over Z_ℓ, δ^3 = 1 forces δ = 1 unless ℓ ≡ 1 mod 3, and the family with a + b = 0 is empty unless ℓ ≡ 1 mod 3.

ideas.what: Rewriting the cocycle equation g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = 1, for ρ an inner automorphism of order 3, as (gR)^3 = R^3. This reduces solving it to classifying elements of GL₂ whose cube is a prescribed scalar.
ideas.modern_name: Nonabelian 1-cocycles of a cyclic group (twisted cube roots); the linear model of the GT 3-cycle relation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard group cohomology; the GT relations are due to Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara
ideas.where_published: Only in the spirit of Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, relations in Sl₂(Ẑ)); not in this explicit form

ideas.what: Explicit classification of solutions in GL(2, Z_ℓ) via Cayley–Hamilton. Either g = -δ'ρ^{-1} (the scalar case), or trace(gR) = δ' with δ^3 = 1, which gives explicit 2-parameter families and a family involving cube roots of unity.
ideas.modern_name: Classification of elements of order 3 (projectively) in GL₂ by trace and determinant

missed.claim: The surrounding pages ask whether every solution of (87) in Sl(2, Ẑ) admits a 'coboundary' parametrization λ₀ρ(λ₀)^{-1}, or a variant of it. That is the question of triviality of a nonabelian H¹(Z/3, Sl₂(Ẑ_ℓ)), with special attention to ℓ = 2. Grothendieck states he does not know the answer.
missed.quote: J'ignore si une g∈Sl(2,Ẑ) ... qui satisfait g ρ(g) ρ²(g)=1 admet une représentation paramétrique de la forme ... λ₀ρ(λ₀)^{-1}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a small, concrete and answerable question about the linear shadow of the GT relations. It is likely settled by standard arguments on conjugacy of order-3 elements, so its novelty is limited.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine but correct (up to slips) linear-algebra classification of the solutions of a twisted cube equation in GL₂(Z_ℓ). It is a working step in Grothendieck's study of the 'équation des lacets', with nothing that a specialist would find unexpected.
transcription_corrections: Case 1° is most likely 'c+d-b = 1/δ' (or a slip of the pen for it) rather than '=1', since the corollary uses d = b - c + 1/δ.
The second family's lower-right entry should read '-δ'u' - c', with δ' = 1/δ.
The crossed-out fragment after the Corollary matrix reads roughly '..., c = (1/(a+b))(a(b+δ'))', an aborted version of the c-formula.

In 2°, the matrix (−1 1; 1 0) together with the factor −δ' is inconsistent with (90) on the previous page, which gives [[-δ',δ'],[-δ',0]]. The bottom-left entry or the sign of the prefactor is probably misread.
